title: Un petit Souper, a la Parisienne (A Family of Sans-Culottes refreshing after the fatigues of the day)
creator: James Gillray
repository: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access, CC0)
citation: James Gillray, "Un petit Souper, a la Parisienne," hand-colored etching, London, 1792. British Museum, Department of Prints and Drawings. Public domain.
alt_text: Colored etching of ragged French sans-culottes cannibalistically feasting on human body parts amid a wrecked room, Gillray's savage satire of the Reign of Terror.

title: The Plumb-pudding in danger; — or — State Epicures taking un Petit Souper
creator: James Gillray
repository: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
citation: James Gillray, "The Plumb-pudding in danger," hand-colored etching, London, 1805. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain.
alt_text: William Pitt and Napoleon Bonaparte seated at a table carving up a globe-shaped plum pudding with swords, each slicing off his share of the world.

title: Capital and Labour
creator: Punch (attributed to John Leech)
citation: "Capital and Labour," Punch, or the London Charivari, vol. 5 (1843). Digitized by HathiTrust. Public domain.
alt_text: Split-scene cartoon contrasting wealthy factory owners lounging in luxury above with emaciated laborers, women, and children toiling in a dark mine below.

title: Pyramid of the Capitalist System
creator: Nedeljkovich, Brashich & Kuharich (International Publishing Co.)
repository: Pre-1929 periodical (Industrial Worker), via Internet Archive
citation: "Pyramid of Capitalist System," issued by Nedeljkovich, Brashich & Kuharich, 1911; reprinted in the Industrial Worker. Public domain.
alt_text: Tiered pyramid cartoon: workers at the base crushed under stacked tiers of capitalists, military, clergy, and monarch, captioned 'we work for all / we feed all.'

title: The White Man's Burden (Apologies to Rudyard Kipling)
creator: Victor Gillam
citation: Victor Gillam, "The White Man's Burden (Apologies to Rudyard Kipling)," Judge, April 1, 1899. Public domain.
alt_text: John Bull and Uncle Sam carrying baskets of caricatured colonized peoples up a steep hill toward 'civilization,' satirizing imperialism's cultural justifications.

title: The Rhodes Colossus: Striding from Cape Town to Cairo
creator: Edward Linley Sambourne
citation: Edward Linley Sambourne, "The Rhodes Colossus," Punch, or the London Charivari, December 10, 1892. Digitized by HathiTrust. Public domain.
alt_text: Cecil Rhodes drawn as a giant straddling the African continent from Cape Town to Cairo, holding a telegraph line, embodying the Scramble for Africa.

title: The British Lion's Vengeance on the Bengal Tiger
creator: John Tenniel
citation: John Tenniel, "The British Lion's Vengeance on the Bengal Tiger," Punch, August 22, 1857. Digitized by HathiTrust. Public domain.
alt_text: A powerful British lion leaping upon a snarling Bengal tiger that stands over a fallen woman and child, a charged British response to the 1857 Indian Rebellion.

title: En Chine — Le gâteau des Rois et... des Empereurs (China — the cake of kings and emperors)
creator: Henri Meyer
citation: Henri Meyer, "En Chine — Le gâteau des Rois et... des Empereurs," Le Petit Journal, January 16, 1898. Public domain.
alt_text: Britain, Germany, Russia, France, and Japan around a pie labeled 'Chine,' knives drawn to carve it up while a Qing official protests, satirizing Western spheres of influence in China.

title: The Chain of Friendship
creator: Unsigned (Brooklyn Daily Eagle)
citation: "The Chain of Friendship," Brooklyn Daily Eagle, 1914. Public domain.
alt_text: A row of national figures each pointing a weapon at the next — Austria at Serbia, Russia at Austria, Germany at Russia, and so on — illustrating how the alliance system dragged Europe into war.

title: Peace and Future Cannon Fodder (The Tiger: 'Curious! I seem to hear a child weeping.')
creator: Will Dyson
citation: Will Dyson, "Peace and Future Cannon Fodder," Daily Herald (London), May 17, 1919. Public domain.
alt_text: The 'Big Four' leaving the Versailles peace talks as Clemenceau (the Tiger) hears a naked weeping child labeled '1940 Class,' foretelling a future war.
